paper.title: Provably Efficient Online RLHF with One-Pass Reward Modeling

settings.name_in_paper: Online RLHF with passive data collection (contextual dueling bandit, Bradley-Terry linear reward)
unmapped: Passive data collection: the triples (x_t, a_t, a_t') are chosen by the environment, not the learner; the learner only outputs a final policy
Output policy is evaluated on contexts drawn from distribution rho; the bound depends on a concentrability coefficient of the collected data
Reward r(x,a) = phi(x,a)^T theta* with known feature map; preference via logistic (Bradley-Terry) link of reward difference
settings.definition_quote: We first consider the passive data collection setting, where the algorithm cannot control the data collection process. At each iteration, the learner obtains $(x_t, a_t, a_t', y_t)$ and updates by Eq.~\eqref{eq:omd}.

settings.name_in_paper: Online RLHF with active data collection
unmapped: Learner actively chooses both the context x and the action pair (a, a') to query from X x A x A
Final policy evaluated on contexts drawn from distribution rho
Reward r(x,a) = phi(x,a)^T theta* with known feature map; Bradley-Terry logistic preference link
settings.definition_quote: At each iteration, we select a triplet $(x_t, a_t, a'_t)$ to query for human feedback $y_t$, and then update the reward model using our one-pass method as defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:omd}.

unmapped: Regret is average-utility regret: sum_t r(x_t, pi*(x_t)) - (r(x_t,a_t)+r(x_t,a_t'))/2
Context generation process is not specified (users provide contexts online); analysis holds for arbitrary context sequences
Reward r(x,a) = phi(x,a)^T theta* with known feature map; Bradley-Terry logistic preference link
settings.definition_quote: we consider the deployment-time adaptation setting, where users provide input contexts in an online manner, and the learner generates responses while simultaneously collecting feedback ... ${\Reg}_T = \sum_{t=1}^T \left(r\left(x_t, \pi^*(x_t)\right)- \frac{1}{2} \left(r\left(x_t, a_t\right) + r\left(x_t, a'_t\right)\right)\right)$

algorithms.name: One-Pass Reward Modeling (OMD with lookahead local norm)

symbols.Phi_H: concentrability coefficient ||E_{x~rho}[phi(x, pi*(x))]||_{H_{T+1}^{-1}}, H_{T+1} = sum_i sigma'(z_i^T theta_{i+1}) z_i z_i^T + lambda I

conditions: linear realizable reward r(x,a)=phi(x,a)^T theta*, ||phi|| <= L, ||theta*|| <= B
tuning: lambda = 84 sqrt(2) eta (d L^2 + B L^3)

source.label: thm:passive
source.quote: Set parameters as in Lemma~\ref{lem:confidence_set}, with probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:passive} ensures ${\subopt}(\pi_{T+1}) = \E_{x \sim \rho} \left[r(x, \pi^*(x)) - r(x, \pi_{T+1}(x))\right] \leq \Ot \left(\sqrt{d} \cdot \bignorm{\mathbb{E}_{x \sim \rho} \left[\phi(x,\pi^*(x))\right]}_{\H_{T+1}^{-1}} \right)$

results.notes: Suboptimality gap of the output policy; data passively collected. Proof gives 2*beta_T*Phi_H with beta_T = O(sqrt(d) log^2(T/delta)). Per-round compute O(1) in t (polynomial in d).

symbols.kappa: non-linearity coefficient: max over x, a, a', theta in Theta of 1/sigma'(phi(x,a)^T theta - phi(x,a')^T theta)

conditions: linear realizable reward r(x,a)=phi(x,a)^T theta*, ||phi|| <= L, ||theta*|| <= B
tuning: lambda = 84 sqrt(2) eta (d L^2 + B L^3)

source.label: thm:active
source.quote: Set parameters as in Lemma~\ref{lem:confidence_set}, with probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:active} ensures $\subopt(\pi_{T+1}) = \E_{x \sim \rho} \left[r(x, \pi^*(x)) - r(x, \pi_{T+1}(x))\right] \leq \Ot \big(d \sqrt{{\kappa}/{T}}\big)$

results.notes: Active query selection maximizing ||phi(x,a)-phi(x,a')||_{H^{-1}} over X x A x A (requires argmax over that set). Per-iteration O(1) in t.

symbols.kappa: non-linearity coefficient: max over x, a, a', theta in Theta of 1/sigma'(phi(x,a)^T theta - phi(x,a')^T theta)

conditions: linear realizable reward r(x,a)=phi(x,a)^T theta*, ||phi|| <= L, ||theta*|| <= B
tuning: lambda = 84 sqrt(2) eta (d L^2 + B L^3)

source.label: thm:deploy
source.quote: For any $\delta \in (0,1]$, set parameters as in Lemma~\ref{lem:confidence_set}, Algorithm~\ref{alg:deploy} ensures the regret satisfies ${\Reg}_T \leq \Ot \big(d\sqrt{{\kappa}{T}}\big)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Regret defined via mean rewards (average of the two chosen actions) vs per-context optimal action, holding w.p. 1-delta. Horizon marked anytime since tuning does not depend on T (beta_t uses t), but the paper does not explicitly claim anytime.
